ls.b_move.title: Moving safely
ls.b_move.sub: Onto squares where you can't be taken
ls.b_move.intro:
Men move forward one diagonal square at a time. After moving, check that an enemy piece cannot jump over it.

A piece is taken when an enemy piece is diagonally in front of it and the square right behind it is empty. A friendly piece behind it keeps it safe.
ls.b_move.goal: Move a piece without giving it away.
ls.b_move.hint: The pieces with a gold ring can move without being taken. Check whether the square right behind the destination is empty.
ls.b_move.ng: After {x} the opponent takes a piece. {m}, for example, was safe.
ls.b_jump.title: Choosing a capture
ls.b_jump.intro:
When you can capture you must, but you may choose which piece captures and how.

If the opponent can take back right away, the gain is gone. Check that the landing square is safe.
ls.b_jump.goal: Choose the capture that gains the most.
ls.b_jump.hint: Capture with the piece with the gold ring and you won't be taken back as easily.
ls.b_jump.ng: After {x} you are taken back. {m} gained the most.
ls.b_multi.title: Multiple jumps
ls.b_multi.sub: Take as many as you can
ls.b_multi.intro:
When you can jump again from the landing square, you keep jumping and take several pieces.

In English checkers, when there are several ways to capture you may choose any of them (you need not take the most). Here, find the move that takes the most.
ls.b_multi.goal: Choose the move that captures the most pieces.
ls.b_multi.hint: Follow the jumps from the piece with the gold ring.
ls.b_king.title: Crowning a king
ls.b_king.intro:
A man that reaches the far row becomes a king. Kings can also move backwards, so they are much stronger than men.

Don't miss a chance to crown — but check that the new king won't be captured at once.
ls.b_king.hint: The piece with the gold ring is one square from the far row.
ls.b_safe.title: Saving a threatened piece
ls.b_safe.intro:
One of your pieces would be taken on the opponent's turn. Move it away, fill the square behind it, or set things up so you can take back.

Turn on "Show pieces under attack" and threatened pieces glow red during games too.
ls.b_safe.goal: Don't let a piece be taken for nothing.
ls.b_safe.hint: Moving a piece with a gold ring loses nothing.
ls.b_safe.ng: After {x} a piece is taken. {m}, for example, saved it.
ls.b_win.title: Finishing the game
ls.b_win.intro:
You win by capturing every enemy piece or leaving the opponent no legal move.

Even with pieces left, a side that cannot move loses. Look for moves that block the enemy pieces too.
ls.b_win.hint: Use the piece with the gold ring to capture everything or leave no move.
ls.b_win.ng: {x} does not win yet. {m} would have won.
ls.t_shot1.title: Shots (2 moves)
ls.t_shot1.intro:
The most important tactic in checkers is the shot. You let the opponent take a piece; since capturing is compulsory, their piece is pulled into place and you then capture several in a row.

"Give one, take two" (the two-for-one) is the basic pattern. Here, find a shot that wins material with your second move.
ls.t_shot1.goal: Find the shot that wins material.
ls.t_shot1.hint: Try moving the piece with the gold ring onto a square where it can be taken.
ls.t_shot1.why: {m} starts the shot: after the opponent's capture you jump back several pieces.
ls.t_shot2.title: Shots (3 moves)
ls.t_shot2.intro:
Longer shots. Because the opponent's captures are forced, you can calculate a sequence that wins material by your third move.

Where you give a piece decides where the enemy piece lands. Picture the landing squares.
ls.t_shot2.goal: Find the move that leads to winning material.
ls.t_shot2.hint: The sequence starts with the piece with the gold ring.
ls.t_defend.title: The only defence
ls.t_defend.intro:
The opponent has a shot in the air, and most moves lose material. Find the one move that holds.

The key to defending: before you move, check that you are not walking into a forced capture.
ls.t_defend.goal: Find the move that loses nothing.
ls.t_defend.hint: Moving the piece with the gold ring is correct.
ls.t_best.title: Finding the winning idea
ls.t_best.intro: Close to the endgame there is one move clearly better than the rest: crowning, stopping an enemy man, winning an exchange… which is it?
ls.t_best.hint: The best move uses the piece with the gold ring.
ls.e_kings.title: King endings
ls.e_kings.intro:
Endings with kings. Even in a won position, few moves keep the win.

Two kings beat one king, but a lone king in a "double corner" (1 and 5, or 28 and 32) takes work to drive out. The answers were checked with the endgame databases.
ls.e_kings.goal: Play a move that keeps the win.
ls.e_kings.hint: Moving a piece with a gold ring keeps the win.
ls.e_kings.ng: {x} lets the win slip. {m} would have won.
ls.e_men.title: Endings with men
ls.e_men.intro:
With men left, the game is decided by who crowns first and by placing pieces to stop the enemy men.

The answers were checked with the endgame databases (up to 4 pieces).
ls.e_men.hint: Moving a piece with a gold ring wins.
ls.e_men.ng: {x} does not win. {m} was the winning move.
ls.e_draw.title: Holding the draw
ls.e_draw.sub: Find the move that does not lose
ls.e_draw.intro:
Even when you are worse, correct play can hold a draw. Usually only one or two moves avoid the loss.

A king hides best in a double corner (1 and 5, or 28 and 32).
ls.e_draw.goal: Play a move that does not lose (holds the draw).
ls.e_draw.hint: Moving a piece with a gold ring holds the draw.
pz.grpEndSub: Winning with few pieces: hunting with kings, and endings with men (position and blocks).
op.grp.a.sub: Openings starting with 11-15, Black's most common first move. The name depends on White's reply.
op.single.intro: Black's 11-15 answered by White's 22-18. The black man on 15 faces the white man on 18, Black must capture 15x22 (captures are compulsory) and White takes back 25x18 — one piece each.
op.cross.intro: Black's 11-15 answered by White's 23-18. The white man on 18 meets the black man on 15 diagonally and threatens 18x11 next; Black has to deal with it.
op.ayrshire.intro: Black's 11-15 answered by White's 24-20 on the side. White develops its side of the board first and leaves the black man on 15 alone for now.
op.old14.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 8-11, 22-17 Black plays 4-8, bringing up a back-row man. One of the most studied classic openings.
op.glasgow.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 8-11, 22-17 Black plays 11-16. The black man on 16 runs into the white men on 19 and 20, and exchanges come quickly.
op.laird.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 8-11, 22-17 Black plays 9-13. The black man on 13 stands in front of the white man on 17, and White answers with moves like 17-14.
op.alma.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 8-11, 22-17 Black plays 3-8, bringing up a back-row man — like the Old Fourteenth (4-8) but with a different back man.
op.souter.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 9-14, 22-17 Black answers 6-9, supporting the man on 14 from 9.
op.fife.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 9-14, 22-17 Black answers 5-9. Like the Souter (6-9) it supports 14, but with the side man from 5.
op.whilter.intro: After 11-15, 23-19, 9-14, 22-17 Black answers 7-11, backing up the man on 15 with 11.
op.edinburgh.intro: Openings starting with Black's 9-13, a move to the side square 13.
op.double.intro: Black's first move 9-14 answered by White's 22-18. The men on 14 and 18 face each other.
op.dcross.intro: Black's first move 9-14 answered by White's 23-18. The men on 14 and 18 meet diagonally and Black must capture 14x23 (captures are compulsory).
op.pioneer.intro: Black 9-14, White 22-17, Black 11-16, White 25-22: both sides gather their men towards the centre.
op.denny.intro: Openings starting with Black's 10-14, advancing towards the centre at 14.
op.kelso.intro: Openings starting with Black's 10-15, taking the central square 15.
op.bristol.intro: Black 11-16, White 24-20, Black 16-19. The black man on 19 comes close to the white camp and exchanges follow easily.
op.bcross.intro: Black 11-16, White 23-18, Black 16-20, White 24-19. The black man goes to the side at 20 while White firms up the centre.
op.dundee.intro: Openings starting with Black's 12-16, bringing the side man on 12 towards the centre at 16.
pz.grpStepSub: Mixed courses: every theme, starting easy and slowly getting longer and harder.
pz.grpTacSub: Shots, multi-jumps, breakthroughs and defence — one theme at a time.
pz.th.combo.sub: Two or three pieces at once
